<reflection>
The high-cat/low-substrate experiment slightly favored M16, M14, M18, M20, M11 - all involving catS or S+catS-related deactivation. M9, M13 (pure cat deactivation) did NOT rise up. This suggests the deactivation is more likely catS-related rather than free-cat-related. The top cluster is very tight though. M7 remains competitive. M5 still poor.

Top candidates: M16 (S+catS→inactive), M14 (catS→inactive), M18 (2catS→inactive), M20 (both cat and catS→inactive), M11 (S+cat→inactive), M7 (two-substrate binding).
</reflection>

<hypothesis>
Now I need to discriminate among catS-related deactivation mechanisms:
- M14: first-order in [catS] only (spontaneous decay).
- M16: bimolecular S+catS (deactivation faster at high [S]).
- M18: bimolecular 2catS (deactivation faster at high [cat]/high [catS]).
- M11: S+cat→inactive (deactivation faster at high [S] when [cat] is free).
- M20: combined.
- M7: no deactivation, but rate has different [S] dependence (2nd order in S at low [S], saturating at high [S]).

Discriminator: Use high substrate concentration with low catalyst. High [S] will:
- M16: accelerate deactivation, low final conversion.
- M11: accelerate deactivation, low final conversion.
- M14: normal deactivation, catS is saturated so same fraction deactivates.
- M18: [catS]^2, but with low [cat], slower deactivation, so higher conversion.
- M7: no deactivation, full conversion expected, and kinetics reflect substrate saturation.

Propose: [S]=3.0, [cat]=0.005, [P]=0.
- If M16 or M11: strong deactivation, very low TON (limited turnovers per cat).
- If M14: moderate deactivation regardless of S.
- If M18: minimal deactivation due to low [cat], high TON.
- If M7: no deactivation, high TON (60x turnover possible).

This differentiates the top candidates well by TON at extreme S/cat ratio.
</hypothesis>
